stimuli.description: simulated office environment with two illuminance levels (200 lx vs. 1000 lx at eye level) at 4000 K CCT

tables.description: Estimated means for baseline comparisons of self-report measures (sleepiness, vitality, tension, happy, sad) across control and fatigue conditions under 200 lx and 1000 lx lighting.
Results of manipulation check for self-report measures (sleepiness, vitality, tension, happy, sad) comparing control and fatigue conditions immediately after manipulation.

Results on subjective (sleepiness, vitality, tension, happy, sad, self-control), performance (PVT, Go-NoGo, 2-Back RTs and % correct), and physiological (heart rate, HRV, SCL) indicators for the Antecedent condition (Fatigue vs. Control) during light exposure.
Results on subjective, performance, and physiological indicators for Lighting condition (200 lx vs. 1000 lx at eye) during light exposure.
Results on subjective evaluations and beliefs concerning the lighting condition and environment.

limitations: The study did not employ EEG or fMRI to measure temporal or spatial modulations in brain activity during the light exposure.
The light exposure was relatively brief (i.e., a half hour) and alertness/vitality after offset of lighting conditions was not measured, so persistence of effects is unknown.
Some measures revealed differences at baseline despite efforts to minimize them, requiring baseline scores as covariates.

The study employed only two light manipulations (200 lx vs. 1000 lx at the eye) and a limited set of performance tasks, limiting generalizability of optimal illuminance levels for different task types.
Task engagement on a first performance task may affect performance on a subsequent task, potentially confounding order effects.
